rv.q: Moment by moment, Bruni has it in great comedic shape, but no palpable human need drives the action and the stakes. Too fun to snooze, though.
An absolute riot — a truly original and genuinely laugh-out-loud story with tight pacing and structure.

The show is positively silly in all the best ways and with Megan Mullally and Nick Offerman surrounded by performers who can more than hold their own with two comedic powerhouses, it's exactly the right final punctuation to put on the Goodman's first one hundred years.
This all means the show comes off as a glitzily produced, exceedingly extended comedy sketch, lacking even the slightest bit of surprise.

Iceboy! or The Completely Untrue Story of How Eugene O’Neill Came to Write “The Iceman Cometh” is an outrageously inventive, joy-charged burst of musical comedy that proves Goodman Theatre can still surprise us in the best possible ways.
With JoAnn M. Hunter’s choreography, a terrific ensemble drives “Iceboy” to a big and satisfying finish and a promising future.
Just in time for summer and a blistering heatwave, ICEBOY is a refreshing escape from the ordinary and predictable.
It's one of the funniest, well-produced comedies of the year.
Flaws notwithstanding, I simply cannot imagine someone not enjoying themselves here.
It’s a frothy nightcap to a year of successful productions, and a nice way to kick off the Goodman’s next act.
This new musical comedy, now enjoying its world premiere as the finale production of the Goodman Theatre’s Centennial season, is a whole lot of fun.
Two acts of silly fun — but despite the whimsy, the production still feels like a work-in-progress, the next draft but perhaps not the final one.

Unfortunately, “Iceboy!” by composer/lyricist Mark Hollmann (“Urinetown”), lyricist/book writer Jay Reiss (“The 25th Annual Putnam County Spelling Bee”) and writer Erin Quinn Purcell is not yet the ideal conduit for the considerable gifts these real-life spouses possess.
But there’s not enough genuine emotional meat on the bones of this show for me.
Iceboy! could follow a similar trajectory—if it tightens up and loses about 20 percent of its overly campy, scatological slapstick.

Iceboy! has Megan Mullally, Nick Offerman, a defrosted caveman, and Eugene O’Neill — and somehow squanders all of it on a forgettable score and a script that never evolves past its own elevator pitch.
Two hours and 25 minutes of sheer beauty in comic storytelling — a comedy that would make Sondheim proud.
Iceboy! is a cheeky romp that is charming, unpredictable, and full of life.
Capturing the feel of traditional musicals while incorporating new writing and comedy, Iceboy! enters into a new era of comedy shows.

cn.t: Critics find Iceboy! a mostly funny, original premise elevated by Mullally and Offerman, but divided on execution—some call it a riot, others say it runs too long and too campy to fully land.
